name: Appeal to Ignorance
shortDef: Concluding a claim is true because it hasn't been proven false, or the reverse.
definition: Treating a lack of evidence as if it were evidence: deciding something is true because no one has disproven it, or false because no one has proven it, when nobody has looked hard enough for the gap to mean much.
howToSpot: Is "no one has shown otherwise" doing the work that real evidence should do?
Has anyone looked in a way that would have found evidence if it existed?
Could the honest answer simply be "we don't know yet"?
classicExample: No one has ever proven that ghosts don't exist, so they must be real.
legitimateVersion: Absence of evidence counts when a thorough search would have found something if it were there, like a full inspection that finds no termite signs in any beam.

contrast.fal_burden_of_proof: Appeal to ignorance draws a conclusion from missing evidence; burden of proof demands that others do the disproving.
contrast.fal_false_dichotomy: Appeal to ignorance treats "not proven false" as "true"; it's like a false dichotomy that leaves out the option "we don't know yet."
